h1:
Chachoengsao 2 Days 1 Night
Temples, Old Markets & the Bang Pakong River
intro: Chachoengsao — locals still call it Paet Riu — sits just over an hour from Bangkok, but the pace drops the moment you arrive. The town keeps things simple: make merit at a temple, wander an old riverside market for Thai-Chinese snacks, then close out the evening by the Bang Pakong River. This is an unhurried 2-day, 1-night plan that actually works on the ground, with rough timings and a budget so you can build it out yourself.

blocks.html: Paet Riu is a great weekend trip when you want out of Bangkok without a long drive. The draws are the town's signature temple, Luang Pho Sothon, where people come from all over to pray, and the old markets along the Bang Pakong River that are still very much alive. This plan keeps day one on temples and the old market, then saves the popular Ganesha temple and souvenir shopping for day two before you head home — a comfortable rhythm that doesn't wear you out.

From Bangkok it's about 1–1.5 hours by car via the motorway or the Bang Na–Trat road. No car? Take the Eastern Line train to Chachoengsao station — tickets run only a few tens of baht — then hop on a songthaew or motorcycle taxi around town. The main sights aren't far apart: Wat Sothon and Ban Mai Market are roughly 5 km from each other, while Wat Saman Rattanaram sits outside town toward Bang Khla district. Having your own car makes everything smoothest.

blocks.title: Pick your day carefully
blocks.html: The 100-year-old Ban Mai Market is busiest on weekends and public holidays, with far more stalls open than on weekdays. For the full atmosphere, time your trip for a weekend — the walk is a lot more fun.

blocks.title: Book the activities in your Chachoengsao trip ahead
blocks.text: Booking online ahead on Klook or GetYourGuide is usually cheaper than the gate and skips the queue. Pick only the experiences you actually want — prices and availability are shown live on each site.

items.label: Day trips from Chachoengsao
items.note: Out and back in a day

blocks.text: Day 1 — Luang Pho Sothon + riverside Ban Mai Market

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Bless at the town temple, walk the old market, graze along the river

items.note: Drive or take the Eastern Line train. Leave buffer for traffic getting out of the city; you'll reach Paet Riu around noon, just in time for lunch.

items.activity: Arrive in Chachoengsao, check in to a riverside stay
items.note: Drop your bags first if the room isn't ready. Riverside stays along the Bang Pakong in town come in a range of prices — pick one near Wat Sothon to keep sightseeing easy.
Try duck noodles or red-pork rice at an old-school shop in town, around 50–80 THB a plate.

items.activity: Pay respects at Luang Pho Sothon, Wat Sothonwararam Worawihan
items.note: The white marble ordination hall on the Bang Pakong River is the town's signature image. Free entry; people pray here for health and good fortune. Dress modestly.

A wooden riverside market in a Thai-Chinese community. Try pak mo (steamed rice rolls), old-style coffee, traditional khanom jeen, and old-fashioned desserts. Easy to graze your way through for a good while.

items.activity: Sunset over the Bang Pakong River
items.note: Find a spot by the water near the market, or head back to your stay. The river looks lovely in the evening and the breeze is cool.
Restaurants along the Bang Pakong serve fresh river prawns and freshwater fish — a relaxed way to close out the day.

blocks.text: Day 2 — Ganesha temple + souvenirs for the road

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Ask Ganesha for a blessing, grab souvenirs, then head home

items.note: Keep it simple — coffee with patongko (fried dough sticks) or congee in town before you set off.

items.activity: Wat Saman Rattanaram, blessings from Ganesha
items.note: The big pink reclining Ganesha sits on a base about 24 m long and 10 m tall, with 32 different Ganesha forms around the base for blessings on work and success. Open 08:00–17:00.

items.activity: Stroll the riverside in front of Wat Saman
items.note: There's a small market of snacks and souvenirs out front. Grab a bite and a cold drink before moving on.
The Bang Khla area has riverside restaurants and cafes worth a stop — a good break before the afternoon.
Paet Riu is known for nam dok mai mangoes in season, moo yor (pork sausage), and Chinese-style pastries (khanom pia). Swing by a souvenir shop in town before you leave.
Leaving in the late afternoon helps you dodge the evening holiday-return traffic; you'll reach Bangkok around evening.

blocks.text: Add these if you have time

items.name: Bang Pakong River cruise
items.blurb: Take a boat to see both banks of the river; in season, some trips look for dolphins near the river mouth. Great for anyone who likes being on the water.

items.name: Khlong Suan 100-year Market
items.blurb: Another old canal-side market that still carries the feel of an old community — easy grazing on Thai-Chinese food. It's over in Ban Pho district.

items.name: Riverside cafes in town
items.blurb: Downtown Paet Riu has cafes right on the Bang Pakong where you can sip coffee with a river view — a nice mid-day break to slot in.

items: 1 night's stay — a guesthouse or riverside hotel runs about ฿600–1,500 per room; split two ways, that's only a few hundred each.
4–5 meals — around ฿400–700 if you stick mostly to street food and the markets.
Getting around town — fuel or songthaews run about ฿200–400, depending on whether you have your own car.
Merit-making + souvenirs — up to you; setting aside ฿300–500 is plenty.

blocks.title: What to wear at the temples
blocks.html: Wat Sothon and Wat Saman are sacred places that draw a lot of visitors. Sleeved tops with knee-covering pants or skirts are respectful and let you in everywhere. Pack an umbrella or hat for the sun too — the temple grounds are fairly open.

faq.q: What should I do in Chachoengsao on a 2-day, 1-night trip?
faq.a: The popular plan is to spend day one paying respects to Luang Pho Sothon at Wat Sothonwararam Worawihan, then walking the 100-year-old Ban Mai Market on the Bang Pakong River, finishing with a riverside dinner. On day two, ask Ganesha for a blessing at Wat Saman Rattanaram and pick up souvenirs before heading home.

faq.q: Is Chachoengsao far from Bangkok, and how do I get there?
faq.a: It's about 1–1.5 hours from Bangkok. Driving via the motorway or the Bang Na–Trat road is easy, or take the Eastern Line train to Chachoengsao station for just a few tens of baht and continue around town from there.

faq.q: What days is Ban Mai Market open?
faq.a: The market is open to walk through, but it's busiest and has the most stalls open on weekends and public holidays. For the fullest atmosphere and the most food, a weekend is your best bet.

faq.q: What time does Wat Saman Rattanaram open?
faq.a: It's open daily, roughly 08:00–17:00. The highlight is the big pink reclining Ganesha, plus 32 different Ganesha forms around the base for blessings on work and success.

faq.q: What souvenirs should I buy in Paet Riu?
faq.a: The local favorites are nam dok mai mangoes in season, moo yor (pork sausage), Chinese-style pastries, and old-fashioned desserts from the markets. You'll find them at souvenir shops in town and in front of the temples.
